title: Erdős 251 coordinate systems: prime-gap sums, dyadic tails, real escape, and free carries

concepts.label: zero-based prime-gap coordinates
concepts.note: The nth-prime and consecutive-gap coordinates used by the #251 development.

concepts.label: finite dyadic partial-sum coordinates
concepts.note: The exact rational partial sums used in finite summation by parts.

concepts.label: real dyadic prime and gap terms
concepts.note: The real term coordinates for the prime and prime-gap series.

concepts.label: rational dyadic tail recurrence
concepts.note: An abstract rational doubling-minus-digit recurrence and its accumulated block.

concepts.label: real tail escape coordinates
concepts.note: The real recurrence and cofinal nonintegral-shift predicate.

concepts.label: rational initial-data orbit
concepts.note: The exact recursively generated rational orbit.

concepts.label: free carry coordinates
concepts.note: The carry coefficients and their finite dyadic partial sums.

concepts.label: proof and interpretation boundary
concepts.note: Lean proves only the cited declarations. Definitions provide representation evidence. The actual real prime-gap tail, its cofinal escape, and Erdős #251 remain open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: prime0 n is the zero-based nth prime and primeGap0 n = prime0 (n+1) - prime0 n. Consecutive primes are monotone, so casting the natural gap to rational numbers gives the exact rational difference.
statement_nodes.engine: definition unfolding plus monotonicity of consecutive primes and exact natural-to-rational subtraction
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard prime indexing and cast normalisation; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These coordinates make no distributional, convergence, rationality, or irrationality claim.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The normalized dyadic partial sum, displayed prime partial sum, forward-difference partial sum, and actual prime-gap partial sum are the exact rational finite-sum coordinates used by the source's summation-by-parts argument.
statement_nodes.engine: exact definitions of four finite rational sums
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finite-sum notation for a standard dyadic summation-by-parts calculation.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The definitions supply neither convergence nor an infinite-series identity; the already-authored theorem nodes in Z17 and Z31 retain those claims.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The real term coordinates are prime0 n / 2^(n+1), prime0 n / 2^n, and primeGap0 n / 2^(n+1); the displayed prime term is exactly twice the normalized prime term.
statement_nodes.engine: definition unfolding and elementary power-of-two arithmetic
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard real-series coordinates; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These term definitions and the factor-two identity prove no summability or irrationality conclusion.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The rational interface consists of the recurrence T_(N+1)=2*T_N-g_(N+1), the shift T_(N+h)-T_N, rational integrality, and the recursively accumulated integer block.
statement_nodes.engine: four exact definitions forming the abstract rational recurrence interface
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary recurrence coordinates; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is an abstract rational recurrence, not the actual infinite prime-gap tail.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For a rational number x and an integer z, x-z is integral if and only if x is integral.
statement_nodes.engine: closure of the integer lattice under integer translation
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This generic arithmetic equivalence does not produce an integral tail shift.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The real interface consists of the real dyadic recurrence, real tail shift, real integrality, and CofinalNonintegralTailShifts, which requires every positive shift to fail integrality cofinally.
statement_nodes.engine: four exact real-valued recurrence and escape definitions
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These definitions do not establish the actual prime-gap real recurrence or cofinal escape; the paper's external prime-number-theorem argument is not formalized here.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any integer digit sequence and rational initial value q, primitive recursion constructs the displayed rational orbit beginning at q, and that orbit satisfies DyadicTailRecurrence exactly.
statement_nodes.engine: primitive recursion and its defining equation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Routine construction of the orbit of an affine recurrence.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This constructs an abstract orbit; it proves neither irrationality nor identification with the actual prime-gap tail.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The free-carry coordinates are the rational and natural coefficients kappa_n=2*K_n-K_(n+1), together with their finite dyadic partial sum.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary carry coordinates; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These definitions alone prove neither the finite telescoping theorem, an infinite limit, nor an aperiodic rational-sum example; Z17 retains the finite identity.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The four finite sums instantiate the zero-based prime and gap coordinates; this relation carries no convergence claim.
The three real terms cast and scale the exact zero-based prime and gap coordinates.
The recurrence's integer block motivates the generic integer-translation equivalence, which by itself produces no integral shift.
Primitive recursion gives one exact orbit satisfying the abstract rational recurrence.
The real interface parallels the rational recurrence while adding a cofinal nonintegrality predicate; no actual prime-gap instantiation is asserted.
The carry coordinates provide a second finite telescoping interface, without an infinite-series or irrationality transport.
